summary: Contestants demonstrate their knowledge of cybersecurity and digital forensics by completing an objective test and Capture the Flag activities. The top 20 advance to create and present a multimedia presentation on tracing crime through cryptocurrency, which is judged on technical content and presentation skills.
time_limits: Round 1: 50-question objective test, no more than sixty (60) minutes
Presentation: three (3) minutes for setup, no more than ten (10) minutes for the presentation, and no more than five (5) minutes for judges’ questions
Presentation will be stopped at seven (7) minutes
submission_requirements: Contestant ID is required for all submissions
Materials from non-registered members and/or those missing Contestant ID cannot be accepted
Contestant is responsible for securing a BPA Release Form(s) from any person, including oneself, whose image or work is used in the project
Contestant is responsible for citing all sources, including oneself, on the Works Cited page for any work used on the project
Materials must follow the organization’s BPA Graphic Standards and make proper use of the BPA logo and/or organization’s name
deadlines: The registration deadline is no later than 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time, on December 1, 2026
competencies: Identify and assess security threats, applying layered security tactics to prevent, detect, and respond to external attacks
Demonstrate knowledge of infrastructure security and organizational security principles to safeguard systems, data, and operations at both a technical and policy level
Apply cryptography, access control, and authentication techniques to protect data integrity, confidentiality, and system access
Harden Windows, Linux, and network devices and services by applying security best practices and configuration controls to reduce vulnerabilities
Demonstrate knowledge of TCP/IP, network defense fundamentals, and wireless technologies to secure and monitor network communications
Develop and implement security policies, conduct risk analysis, and configure router and access control lists to establish and enforce organizational security standards
Demonstrate knowledge of Internet security issues and biometrics as they apply to identity verification and web-based threat mitigation
Manage certificates and monitor security infrastructure to maintain compliance, ensure system integrity, and respond to emerging threats

rubric.criterion: Contestant followed Copyright and/or Fair Use Guidelines and the Artificial Intelligence Usage & Citation Policy.

rubric.description: The introduction is engaging and well-structured, and the summary provides a clear, insightful wrap-up that reinforces key findings.
Objectives are precise, well-articulated, and demonstrate a strong understanding of the project’s purpose.
Technical terms are used accurately and effectively, with clear explanations that enhance communication and demonstrate depth of knowledge.
Demonstrates strong understanding with consistently accurate, detailed, and insightful content.
Typography and graphics are thoughtfully designed, enhancing both clarity and the progression of ideas.
Charts and graphs are well-integrated, visually clear, and enhance understanding through effective data presentation.
Voice is confident and engaging, with precise diction that enhances clarity and professionalism.
Shows strong presence with confident delivery, assertive communication, and engaging eye contact that supports audience connection.
The theme is thoroughly developed with strong coherence, depth, and consistent alignment to the topic.
Responses are detailed, insightful, and effectively address the judges' questions.
Setup lasted no longer than three (3) minutes, and the presentation lasted no more than seven (7) minutes.

judging_notes: Judges’ comments will be returned digitally through the online judging system at the national level.
Materials submitted for technical judging will not be returned and will not be available at NLC.
Props and/or additional items shall not be used as a basis for scoring.
Presentation will be stopped at seven (7) minutes.
eligibility_notes: Any middle level, secondary or postsecondary contestant may enter this event.
There are no restrictions on the number of entries per chapter or per state.

Contestants who do not submit an entry following the topic listed or do not follow the Copyright and/or Fair Use Guidelines and the Artificial Intelligence Usage and Citation Policy will be disqualified.
Contestants participating in the competition must be registered for the event prior to the submission deadline to be eligible.
